source_text: Unde mihi accidit tantae contumeliae dignitas? Nihil in me tale conferre laudando potuisses. Sensa mea dicis esse reprobanda, sed Dei opera damnanda; me male disputare; sed Deum nequiter creare pronuntias, me errare clamas; illum saevire, me asseris nescire legem; Deum vero nescire iustitiam; me vociferaris catholicum non esse, quod dicam Christum provocare quos salvet; Deum vero iuras creare quos damnet, nec ob aliud condere, nisi ut eant omnes in condemnationem.
pass_a_gloss: Whence has the dignity of so great an insult happened to me? You could have conferred nothing such on me by praising. You say my senses are to be reproved, but the works of God to be condemned; that I dispute badly; but you pronounce that God creates wickedly, you cry that I err; that he rages, you assert that I do not know the law; but that God does not know justice; you vociferate that I am not catholic, because I say that Christ provokes those whom he may save; but you swear that God creates those whom he may damn, nor founds them for another thing, except that all go into condemnation.
pass_b_english: How did I come to deserve the dignity of so great an insult? By praising me you could have bestowed nothing like it. You say my views deserve rejection, but God's works deserve condemnation. You declare that I argue badly, but that God creates wickedly. You shout that I err, but that he is cruel. You assert that I do not know the Law, but that God does not know justice. You cry out that I am not catholic because I say Christ calls people in order to save them; but you swear that God creates people to condemn them, and brings them into being for no other reason than that all should go into condemnation (compare Romans 5:18) (Romans 5:18).

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
